# rollout-gate Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Rollout gate: Decide, as a DMN decision table with hit policy FIRST, whether a kappa-registry platform may roll out, from its conformance verdict, its signing key backup, its data backup, whether its environment is pinned and whether its images were admitted.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never go when key is missing

The app SHALL NOT answer `go` when key is missing, because never roll out a node whose identity could be lost.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal missing complete pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `go`
- **AND** the app answers `no-go`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never go when conformance is untested

The app SHALL NOT answer `go` when conformance is untested, because never roll out an untested registry.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `untested backed-up complete pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `go`
- **AND** the app answers `hold`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never go when backup is not complete

The app SHALL NOT answer `go` when backup is not complete, because never roll out without a complete backup.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal backed-up partial pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `go`
- **AND** the app answers `hold`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Always no-go when conformance is nonconformant

The app SHALL answer `no-go` when conformance is nonconformant, because a nonconformant registry is always no-go.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `nonconformant backed-up complete pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `no-go`
- **AND** the app answers `no-go`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-001 no-go when key is missing

The app SHALL answer `no-go` when key is missing, because kappa-registry README: losing the signing key loses every capability edge, delegation chain and epoch signature.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal missing complete pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `no-go`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 no-go when conformance is nonconformant

The app SHALL answer `no-go` when conformance is nonconformant and no earlier rule matches, because a MUST failure means clients cannot rely on the protocol.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `nonconformant backed-up complete pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `no-go`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 no-go when images is refused

The app SHALL answer `no-go` when images is refused and no earlier rule matches, because a workload whose image was refused cannot run.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal backed-up complete pinned refused` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `no-go`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 hold when conformance is untested

The app SHALL answer `hold` when conformance is untested and no earlier rule matches, because an untested registry is unproven, not broken.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `untested backed-up complete pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `hold`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 hold when backup is not complete

The app SHALL answer `hold` when backup is not complete and no earlier rule matches, because kappa-registry README: back up blobs/, state.redb and keys/.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal backed-up partial pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `hold`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 hold when env is drifting

The app SHALL answer `hold` when env is drifting and no earlier rule matches, because kappa-distribution CLAUDE.md: the toolchain is hermetic via Nix, so a drifting one cannot reproduce the build.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal backed-up complete drifting admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `hold`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: Otherwise go

The app SHALL answer `go` when no rule matches, because conformant, keyed, backed up, pinned and admitted.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal backed-up complete pinned admitted` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `go`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `ideal backed-up complete drifting refused`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `no-go`, decided by REQ-003, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 5 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `go`, `hold`, `no-go`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conformance` | `ideal`, `conformant`, `nonconformant`, `untested` | the conformance verdict of the registry |
| `key` | `backed-up`, `missing` | whether the node's Ed25519 signing key in keys/ is backed up |
| `backup` | `complete`, `partial`, `none` | whether blobs/ and state.redb are backed up |
| `env` | `pinned`, `drifting` | whether the toolchain is pinned by a Nix flake lock |
| `images` | `admitted`, `refused` | whether every image the rollout needs was admitted |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `go` | ready to roll out |
| `hold` | nothing is broken, but something is unproven or unprotected; fix it and ask again |
| `no-go` | something is broken that a rollout would make worse |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 5 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- It decides from the verdicts the other apps give; it runs none of them.
- Budget and staffing are outside it.

## Examples

- `ideal backed-up complete pinned admitted` gives `go`
- `conformant backed-up complete pinned admitted` gives `go`
- `ideal missing complete pinned admitted` gives `no-go`
- `nonconformant backed-up complete pinned admitted` gives `no-go`
- `ideal backed-up complete pinned refused` gives `no-go`
- `untested backed-up complete pinned admitted` gives `hold`
- `ideal backed-up partial pinned admitted` gives `hold`
- `ideal backed-up complete drifting admitted` gives `hold`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.

- `prism/spec.json` is this spec as data.
- `src/RolloutGate.lex.tex` is the LexLean model generated from it. It is the single source of the app.
